# F8 wording log: process language removed from reader-facing text (rc-data, 2026-10-25)

Finding F8 (P1): provenance notes, map notes and not-drawn "Research notes", summaries, coverage rows and source notes showed internal worklog language ("REVIEW REQUIRED (A17)", "fetched this session", "WebSearch", "Second pass", "integrator", "agent", "workstream", "dangling reference ... until that lead lands", "validator", amendment ids). Companion to `RELEASE_RC_DATA.md`. No value, quote, source, date, status, confidence, coordinate, interval or name was changed by this sweep (checked by comparing every changed file against the commit before: only string fields of the kinds listed below differ, 0 non-string differences; `kind` changed on two sites, see the main log).

Reason for every entry: process language removed or replaced by a plain statement of the evidence and its limits; no new evidence is introduced, so no source or quote is attached (dates inside the new text are the `verified_at` / `accessed` / `date` of the value the note sits on).

## How it was done

1. Deterministic pass (634 strings in 327 files, commit `dccc200`): regular expressions for the templated sentences.
   - CMS member rows (244): "CMS's own institutions/collaboration page requires a CMS e-group login and could not be fetched publicly; this row rests on the affiliation list of a CMS Collaboration paper from <month year>, which the ontology allows as an alternative to an official roster." became "CMS's own institution list is behind a CMS login and is not public; this row rests on the affiliation list of a CMS Collaboration paper from <month year>."
   - Notes consisting only of "Derived field(s) ... deliberately not written/authored (v0.2 A1)" were deleted (reviewer boilerplate about the data model).
   - "(integrator, 2026-09-21, per docs/atlas-worklog/GEOMETRY_*.md)" became "(2026-09-21)".
   - "Operating interval; the single sourced row was split from its terminal event (A3, date)" became "Operating interval; the terminal event is its end."; "Terminal event derived from the end of the same sourced interval (A3, date)" became "Terminal event: the end of the operating interval above."
   - Parenthesised amendment ids "(A17)", "(A15/A25)", "(v0.2 A1)" were removed; "flagged for review" removed; "Checks done in the worklog:" became "Check:"; "see the worklog ..." tails removed.
2. Hand rewrite in 8 groups (g1 experiments A-M, g2 experiments N-Z, g3 collaborations, g4 detectors/accelerators/beamlines, g5 sites, g6 geometry, g7 maps/facilities/institutions, g8 coverage/results/documents/sources), 1,503 flagged strings, then 3 groups (g9-g11) for 94 change-log labels ("CORRECTED 2026-09-18", "REWRITTEN ... (before: ...)", "END ADDED", "Verification fix", "Gaps stream", "owned by ..."), then group g12 (25 strings, lead). Each edit went through an apply tool that checks the old text, refuses edits that keep process wording and logs old -> new. Rules: keep the substance (what is known, evidence strength, what would settle it); dates only from the record; delete stale cross-references after checking that the referenced record exists.
3. Direct edits by the lead: `site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1` and `site:fermilab-main-campus` (kind and notes, see the main log); stale coordinate statements in the CDF/D0, LNGS Hall B, ECN3 and SPS LSS4/LSS5 site records; the Baksan and Boulby map notes; "sources fetched" wording in 14 records. Their old -> new strings are in the git history (commits `c743bc9`, `9cdd2b5`).

Counts per group (apply-tool entries): g1 191, g2 160, g3 272, g4 255, g5 133, g6 137, g7 154, g8 239, g9 35, g10 31, g11 28, g12 25. A `new: null` entry is a deleted `notes[]` item or `missing_fields` item (a note that was only a stale cross-reference, a change log or a data-model remark).

Statements found to be stale or wrong while rewriting (wording was corrected to what the record shows; sources untouched) are listed in each group's report; the main ones: Pierre Auger status note; SHiP approval source; P-ONE STRAW "is taking data"; Project 8 phase status; NOvA "continues to operate"; DONUT 800 GeV note; LZ/boulby reference; CEBAF, SLAC linac and PSI-HIPA interval notes; the CDF/D0/LNGS/ECN3/SPS site coordinate statements. Open items for a later pass (not process language): `auger-sd750-infill-boundary` cites no valid source for the 23.5 km2 infill area; `detectors/kamland.json` notes say Wikipedia-only specs while its technology note cites a paper; `result:cms-lhcb-bs-to-mumu-observation-2015` links only CMS; `result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006` omits SLD; `site:desy-hera-south-hall-zeus` still carries the campus centroid.

**data/atlas/geometry/auger-sd1500-stations-band-01.json**
- `/method`: 80 of the 1587 active main-array stations: the active sd1500 stations sorted by northing from north to south and split into 20 consecutive groups of 79 or 80, so that each record stays within 400 vertices; this group lies between UTM northing 6129.5 km and 6134.7 km. Station positions are the northing and easting columns of sdMap.csv in the Pierre Auger Collaboration Open Data release 3 (20 March 2024, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10488964), which the Collaboration describes as "UTC" [sic] coordinates in metres (the data page does not state the zone or datum). They are read as UTM zone 19 south (central meridian 69 deg W) on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (EPSG:32719) because only zone 19 puts the numbers at Malargue (the converted stations span latitude 34.93 to 35.52 S and longitude 68.91 to 69.66 W), and WGS 84 is the GPS datum; this reading is this work's assumption, hence confidence approximate and accuracy_m 50. Only stations the release marks as still in operation (stop = 1) are drawn; 53 stations with a recorded stop time are not. Each station is drawn as a 3.6 m square centred on its position, aligned to true north: the tank diameter of 3.6 m is from the Observatory paper (arXiv:1502.01323 section 3.1), so the marker has the real tank size, not the tank outline. Check done in the worklog: nearest-neighbour distance of the 1587 active sd1500 stations has a median of 1489.5 m against the official triangular grid of 1500 m (arXiv:1502.01323 section 1); station altitudes in the table run 1344 m to 1619 m against the official 1340 m to 1610 m. → 80 of the 1587 active main-array stations: the active sd1500 stations sorted by northing from north to south and split into 20 consecutive groups of 79 or 80, so that each record stays within 400 vertices; this group lies between UTM northing 6129.5 km and 6134.7 km. Only stations the release marks as still in operation (stop = 1) are drawn; 53 stations with a recorded stop time are not. Station positions are the northing and easting columns of sdMap.csv in the Pierre Auger Collaboration Open Data release 3 (20 March 2024, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10488964), which the Collaboration describes as "UTC" [sic] coordinates in metres (the data page does not state the zone or datum). They are read as UTM zone 19 south (central meridian 69 deg W) on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (EPSG:32719) because only zone 19 puts the numbers at Malargue (the converted stations span latitude 34.93 to 35.52 S and longitude 68.91 to 69.66 W), and WGS 84 is the GPS datum; this reading is this work's assumption, hence confidence approximate and accuracy_m 50. Only stations the release marks as still in operation (stop = 1) are drawn; 53 stations with a recorded stop time are not. Each station is drawn as a 3.6 m square centred on its position, aligned to true north: the tank diameter of 3.6 m is from the Observatory paper (arXiv:1502.01323 section 3.1), so the marker has the real tank size, not the tank outline. Check done in the worklog: nearest-neighbour distance of the 1587 active sd1500 stations has a median of 1489.5 m against the official triangular grid of 1500 m (arXiv:1502.01323 section 1); station altitudes in the table run 1344 m to 1619 m against the official 1340 m to 1610 m. → 79 of the 1587 active main-array stations: the active sd1500 stations sorted by northing from north to south and split into 20 consecutive groups of 79 or 80, so that each record stays within 400 vertices; this group lies between UTM northing 6100.9 km and 6103.5 km. Each station is drawn as a 3.6 m square centred on its position, aligned to true north: the tank diameter of 3.6 m is from the Observatory paper (arXiv:1502.01323 section 3.1), so the marker has the real tank size, not the tank outline. Check: nearest-neighbour distance of the 71 active sd750 stations has a median of 742.7 m against the official 750 m spacing (arXiv:1502.01323 abstract).

**data/atlas/geometry/icecube-deepcore-strings-79-86.json**
- `/method`: Plan positions of the eight specialised DeepCore strings, from the same IC86 geometry file, frame and anchor as geometry:icecube-strings-1-78 (each string drawn as a 2 m square marker; positions are the mean horizontal (x, y) of the 60 DOMs, identical for every DOM). Frame and anchor: the IceCube coordinate system has its y-axis along the Prime Meridian (Grid North, towards Greenwich) and its x-axis 90 degrees clockwise from it (Grid East) (IceCube instrumentation paper, arXiv v3, section 5.3), and its origin is at elevation 883.9 m. The IceCube Collaboration software repository i3astropy gives the nominal location of the centre of the detector as lat -89.9944, lon -62.6081, height 883.9 m, which is taken as the frame origin. Conversion: the origin is placed at that point in a South Pole azimuthal-equidistant plane (distance from the pole = colatitude x 6 371 008.8 m, grid north = 0 deg meridian, grid east = 90 deg E; this is the same plane the browser draws), each string is the origin plus its (x, y) offset, and the inverse projection gives lat/lon. The origin is 622.7 m from the pole on the 62.6 deg W meridian. Accuracy: the layout of the strings relative to each other is surveyed to about 1 m, and the pattern keeps its true size and orientation (grid north). The absolute position of the whole pattern is only good to about 500 m: the anchor is a nominal value of no stated epoch, the array moves with the ice about 10 m a year relative to geographic coordinates, and the lat/lon of IceCube on Wikipedia and in OpenStreetMap (89.99 S, 63.4531 W) lies 489 m from the anchor used. Check done in the worklog: Delaunay edges shorter than 110 m between the 15 DeepCore strings (these 8 plus the seven central standard strings 26, 27, 35, 36, 37, 45, 46) span 40.9 m to 104.9 m against the official range of 41 m to 105 m; the median of all 36 edges is 71.8 m against the official average of 72 m. → Plan positions of the eight specialised DeepCore strings, from the same IC86 geometry file, frame and anchor as geometry:icecube-strings-1-78 (each string drawn as a 2 m square marker; positions are the mean horizontal (x, y) of the 60 DOMs, identical for every DOM). **data/atlas/geometry/hanbit-core-r1.json**
- `/geometry/note` (worklog pointer removed): Reactor containment building at the Hanbit (Yonggwang) Nuclear Power Plant, identified in OSM by power=generator, generator:source=nuclear. Assignment to reactor number R1 (of 6, numbered geographically southwest to northeast) is inferred from which numbering direction gives the best nonlinear least-squares fit of the RENO proposal's own per-reactor near/far detector distances (arXiv:1003.1391 Table 1.2) against these six OSM building positions (residuals under 6 m on distances of 300-1560 m for this SW-to-NE numbering, versus hundreds of metres for the reverse numbering or any other reactor-to-building permutation); see geometry:reno-near-detector method and the worklog. The table itself does not give reactor coordinates, only the SW-NE physical order of the six buildings is used, not a claim about which specific numbered unit (Hanbit's own operator-assigned Unit 1-6 numbering) each is. → Reactor containment building at the Hanbit (Yonggwang) Nuclear Power Plant, identified in OpenStreetMap by power=generator, generator:source=nuclear. The assignment to reactor number R1 (of 6, numbered geographically southwest to northeast) is inferred from which numbering direction gives the best nonlinear least-squares fit of the RENO proposal's per-reactor near/far detector distances (arXiv:1003.1391 Table 1.2) against these six OpenStreetMap building positions: residuals are under 6 m on distances of 300-1560 m for the southwest-to-northeast numbering, versus hundreds of metres for the reverse numbering or any other reactor-to-building permutation (the fit is described on the RENO near-detector point). The table gives no reactor coordinates; only the southwest-to-northeast physical order of the six buildings is used. This is not a claim about which of Hanbit's operator-assigned Units 1-6 each building is.

**data/atlas/geometry/icecube-array-footprint.json**
- `/method` (validator and 'computed here' wording removed): Convex hull of the 78 standard string positions of geometry:icecube-strings-1-78 (13 corner vertices, each straight edge subdivided into pieces of 10 m or less in the grid plane so that the validator's longitude-latitude area formula, which is only exact for short edges near the pole, measures the true area). It is an outline computed here to show the footprint of the 1 km3 volume, not a published boundary of the instrumented ice. Frame and anchor: the IceCube coordinate system has its y-axis along the Prime Meridian (Grid North, towards Greenwich) and its x-axis 90 degrees clockwise from it (Grid East) (IceCube instrumentation paper, arXiv v3, section 5.3), and its origin is at elevation 883.9 m. The IceCube Collaboration software repository i3astropy gives the nominal location of the centre of the detector as lat -89.9944, lon -62.6081, height 883.9 m, which is taken as the frame origin. Conversion: the origin is placed at that point in a South Pole azimuthal-equidistant plane (distance from the pole = colatitude x 6 371 008.8 m, grid north = 0 deg meridian, grid east = 90 deg E; this is the same plane the browser draws), each string is the origin plus its (x, y) offset, and the inverse projection gives lat/lon. The origin is 622.7 m from the pole on the 62.6 deg W meridian. Accuracy: the layout of the strings relative to each other is surveyed to about 1 m, and the pattern keeps its true size and orientation (grid north). The absolute position of the whole pattern is only good to about 500 m: the anchor is a nominal value of no stated epoch, the array moves with the ice about 10 m a year relative to geographic coordinates, and the lat/lon of IceCube on Wikipedia and in OpenStreetMap (89.99 S, 63.4531 W) lies 489 m from the anchor used. → Convex hull of the 78 standard string positions of the IceCube strings 1-78 feature (13 corner vertices, each straight edge subdivided into pieces of 10 m or less in the grid plane so that an area calculation on longitude-latitude coordinates, which is only exact for short edges near the pole, measures the true area).
